chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Safwan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A slave is owned by partners, and one of them sold his share. Then one of them said, 'I have more right to him.' Is that so? He said, 'Yes, if he is single.'

key_terms.اَلْمَمْلُوكُ: The slave (male or female), object of ownership

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of pre-emption (shuf'ah) for co-owners of a slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the conditions of *shuf'ah* (pre-emption) regarding the sale of a co-owned slave, with Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifying that the right applies when the slave is 'single' (*wahidan*), a term scholars interpret as being free from marital bonds that might complicate ownership division. It highlights the practical application of pre-emption in preventing unwanted third parties from entering the co-ownership structure, a principle rooted in maintaining harmony among partners. The narration underscores the precision of Shia jurisprudence in distinguishing between different types of property rights and their associated pre-emption rules.
